subject: Intermittent 502/504 from /v2/query since 18:15 UTC (logs attached inline)
body:
Hello,

We are seeing intermittent failures on the Kestrel query API in production, starting around 18:15 UTC on June 25. Our own service depends on it to render analytics inside our product, so our end customers are seeing empty charts and error banners.

Summary
- Endpoint: POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query
- Symptom: HTTP 502 or 504, roughly one request out of three
- Before: error rate below 0.1% over the last three months
- Our client library: kestrel-python 3.2.1, default timeout 30s, 2 retries with exponential backoff
- Region: eu-west

Example request (values anonymised):

curl -X POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KESTREL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dataset":"orders","metrics":["revenue"],"group_by":["month"],"limit":100}'

Typical failing response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","message":"upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers","request_id":"req_req_470cd0d5"}}

Excerpt of our client-side log (UTC):

2026-08-04T14:36:29Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_c6441703 latency=9523ms
2026-08-24T08:25:34Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_31cf438e latency=27935ms

2026-08-08T07:47:18Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_645cb103 latency=7948ms

What we verified
- The problem is not tied to a specific dataset, we see it on 4 different datasets.
- It is not tied to payload size: tiny queries (limit 1) fail as well.
- It is not our network: the same request from three different networks behaves identically.
- Your status page shows all systems operational, which doesn't match what we observe.
- The retries help a bit but with three attempts we still get about 4% failures for end users.

We need to know whether this is a known incident and what the expected resolution time is, because we have to decide whether to put a maintenance banner in our product. Please also let us know if there's something we should change on our side (timeouts, concurrency).

For context, this is the third time in a few months that we run into something like this, and each time it took several days to get resolved. I'm not saying this to complain, I would just like to know whether there is a better channel for issues that affect production.

Some of the data involved is confidential, so if you need samples please tell us how to send them securely rather than by email.

Please note that James Dubois from our team is also following this ticket and may reply from a different address. Feel free to include them.

Thanks,
Ruth Patel

Hello,

I am writing on behalf of the finance team at Granite Peak Mining. Since we were upgraded to version 5.1 on June 22, our nightly CSV export has been failing, and I would like to give you as much detail as possible so that nobody has to ask us for it later.

What we do
Every night at 02:00 a scheduled job exports the "Finance Summary" dataset (5,400 rows, 38 columns) to CSV. The file is picked up by our accounting system at 06:00 and used to reconcile payments. This has worked without a problem for more than a year.

What happens now
1. The job starts normally at 02:00.
2. After roughly 30 seconds the export fails with a 500 error.
3. The UI shows "Export failed, please try again later" and nothing is written to our storage bucket.
4. Clicking "Retry" produces the same result. Exporting manually from the dashboard fails the same way for anything above about 20,000 rows.

Environment
- Plan: Free
- Workspace region: EU
- Browser used for manual tests: Firefox 128
- Data source: Stripe
- Number of users affected: 3 (everyone who relies on the nightly file)

Relevant lines from the export log shown in the Admin > Jobs page:

subject: Performance regression on dashboards since June 28 (measurements included)
body:
Hi team,

Since around June 28 our dashboards have become a lot slower. I measured a few of them so that you have numbers rather than "it feels slow". Everything below was measured in Firefox 128, on a wired connection, with the browser cache cleared before each run, and the times are how long it takes until the last widget stops showing the loading spinner.

| Dashboard | Widgets | Time before (ms) | Time now (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regional Revenue | 3 | 4000 | 45000 |
| Regional Revenue | 3 | 2000 | 48000 |
| Support Backlog | 7 | 4000 | 24000 |
| Marketing Funnel | 3 | 2000 | 19000 |
| Support Backlog | 8 | 2000 | 48000 |
| Marketing Funnel | 4 | 5000 | 52000 |
| Support Backlog | 6 | 4000 | 12000 |
| Marketing Funnel | 8 | 2000 | 25000 |

Observations:
- The slowdown is much larger for dashboards with several widgets that use the same HubSpot data source.
- Dashboards that use uploaded CSV files are not affected at all.
- Opening a single widget in the editor and running its query is fast (under 2 seconds). It seems that the problem occurs when several widgets load at the same time, as if the queries were executed one after another instead of in parallel.
- The browser's network tab shows the requests to /api/widgets/query being started at almost the same time but the responses arriving one by one, about every 4 seconds.
- I checked with two colleagues in different offices and they see the same behaviour, so it isn't my machine or network.

What I'd like: confirmation of whether something changed on your side around that date (a new release or a change to query concurrency limits for our plan) and whether there is a setting we can change. If you need HAR files I can export them, but they contain our internal hostnames so I'd need to know how to send them securely.

It's not blocking us, people can still work, but the morning stand-up used to start with these dashboards and we now wait almost a minute for them.

Timeline: first noticed on June 28, reported internally on Tuesday, and this ticket was written after we ruled out changes on our side. Nothing else was deployed in that window apart from routine operating system updates.

Please note that Leila Petrov from our team is also following this ticket and may reply from a different address. Feel free to include them.

We understand that you receive many requests. We are not asking for an immediate fix, only for a clear indication of where this stands and what we can expect.

Thanks a lot,
Carlos Lambert
Granite Peak Mining

subject: Intermittent 502/504 from /v2/query since 09:30 UTC (logs attached inline)
body:
Hello,

We are seeing intermittent failures on the Kestrel query API in production, starting around 09:30 UTC on July 14. Our own service depends on it to render analytics inside our product, so our end customers are seeing empty charts and error banners.

Summary
- Endpoint: POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query
- Symptom: HTTP 502 or 504, roughly one request out of three
- Before: error rate below 0.1% over the last three months
- Our client library: kestrel-python 3.2.1, default timeout 30s, 2 retries with exponential backoff
- Region: eu-west

Example request (values anonymised):

curl -X POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KESTREL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dataset":"orders","metrics":["revenue"],"group_by":["month"],"limit":100}'

Typical failing response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","message":"upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers","request_id":"req_req_c64077d9"}}

Excerpt of our client-side log (UTC):

2026-08-14T00:05:13Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_c911dbc6 latency=6423ms
2026-08-19T16:21:11Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_67cb38fd latency=6301ms
2026-08-18T17:32:02Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_5f5039d4 latency=18653ms
2026-08-27T11:52:44Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_130b6383 latency=1506ms
2026-08-28T21:09:39Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_bc09a90f latency=30000ms
2026-08-17T23:44:36Z 200 POST /v2/query request_id=req_17a38636 latency=120ms
2026-08-16T14:56:54Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_89e94563 latency=30000ms
2026-08-25T05:10:29Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_9ea8db1d latency=4893ms
2026-08-24T03:49:35Z 200 POST /v2/query request_id=req_9afa9ce0 latency=94ms
2026-08-13T15:26:01Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_cb5f26e5 latency=8630ms
2026-08-23T03:51:24Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_786b6a78 latency=7710ms
2026-08-10T19:52:59Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_b9804cc1 latency=30000ms
2026-08-24T10:12:31Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_3b25224c latency=4990ms
2026-08-11T11:52:31Z 200 POST /v2/query request_id=req_232b7c4b latency=162ms
2026-08-04T07:44:08Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_9c29ca36 latency=12557ms

What we verified
- The problem is not tied to a specific dataset, we see it on 4 different datasets.
- It is not tied to payload size: tiny queries (limit 1) fail as well.
- It is not our network: the same request from three different networks behaves identically.
- Your status page shows all systems operational, which doesn't match what we observe.
- The retries help a bit but with three attempts we still get about 4% failures for end users.

We need to know whether this is a known incident and what the expected resolution time is, because we have to decide whether to put a maintenance banner in our product. Please also let us know if there's something we should change on our side (timeouts, concurrency).

We understand that you receive many requests. We are not asking for an immediate fix, only for a clear indication of where this stands and what we can expect.

For context, this is the third time in a few months that we run into something like this, and each time it took several days to get resolved. I'm not saying this to complain, I would just like to know whether there is a better channel for issues that affect production.

Thanks,
Lena Lambert
Tidewater Bank

subject: Intermittent 502/504 from /v2/query since 00:00 UTC (logs attached inline)
body:
Hello,

We are seeing intermittent failures on the Kestrel query API in production, starting around 00:00 UTC on July 19. Our own service depends on it to render analytics inside our product, so our end customers are seeing empty charts and error banners.

Summary
- Endpoint: POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query
- Symptom: HTTP 502 or 504, roughly one request out of three
- Before: error rate below 0.1% over the last three months
- Our client library: kestrel-python 3.2.1, default timeout 30s, 2 retries with exponential backoff
- Region: eu-west

Example request (values anonymised):

curl -X POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KESTREL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dataset":"orders","metrics":["revenue"],"group_by":["month"],"limit":100}'

Typical failing response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","message":"upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers","request_id":"req_req_8827d6d3"}}

Excerpt of our client-side log (UTC):

2026-08-07T23:24:25Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_2f46e215 latency=3428ms
2026-08-18T23:58:54Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_4ae20655 latency=30000ms
2026-08-27T16:52:29Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_af4dcabb latency=27129ms
2026-08-10T19:18:27Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_9f68d484 latency=8922ms
2026-08-15T07:33:37Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_13d4536e latency=4239ms
2026-08-22T09:54:51Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_c0a68815 latency=8771ms
2026-08-14T17:24:12Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_8abd43e7 latency=13367ms
2026-08-09T18:38:32Z 502 GET  /v2/datasets request_id=req_13aa80a4 latency=4688ms
2026-08-04T13:54:49Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_91153f93 latency=26357ms
2026-08-20T20:27:04Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_f4f14e67 latency=30000ms
2026-08-18T13:28:25Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_72a9e10d latency=6018ms
2026-08-24T06:26:10Z 502 POST /v2/query request_id=req_3debf9a6 latency=27671ms
2026-08-01T01:22:15Z 200 POST /v2/query request_id=req_e39065b6 latency=328ms
2026-08-15T23:06:32Z 504 POST /v2/query request_id=req_e97f48a4 latency=30000ms

What we verified
- The problem is not tied to a specific dataset, we see it on 4 different datasets.
- It is not tied to payload size: tiny queries (limit 1) fail as well.
- It is not our network: the same request from three different networks behaves identically.
- Your status page shows all systems operational, which doesn't match what we observe.
- The retries help a bit but with three attempts we still get about 4% failures for end users.

We need to know whether this is a known incident and what the expected resolution time is, because we have to decide whether to put a maintenance banner in our product. Please also let us know if there's something we should change on our side (timeouts, concurrency).

Please note that Yuki Sato from our team is also following this ticket and may reply from a different address. Feel free to include them.

Our team is spread over three time zones, so a written answer is more useful than a call. If a call is really needed, mornings (CET) work best.

We understand that you receive many requests. We are not asking for an immediate fix, only for a clear indication of where this stands and what we can expect.

Some of the data involved is confidential, so if you need samples please tell us how to send them securely rather than by email.

Thanks,
Sara Novak
Verdant Farms

body:
Hello,

I am writing on behalf of the finance team at Nimbus Telecom. Since we were upgraded to version 4.14 on July 25, our nightly CSV export has been failing, and I would like to give you as much detail as possible so that nobody has to ask us for it later.

What we do
Every night at 02:00 a scheduled job exports the "Finance Summary" dataset (18,000 rows, 38 columns) to CSV. The file is picked up by our accounting system at 06:00 and used to reconcile payments. This has worked without a problem for more than a year.

What happens now
1. The job starts normally at 02:00.
2. After roughly 30 seconds the export fails with a 500 error.
3. The UI shows "Export failed, please try again later" and nothing is written to our storage bucket.
4. Clicking "Retry" produces the same result. Exporting manually from the dashboard fails the same way for anything above about 20,000 rows.

Environment
- Plan: Business
- Workspace region: EU
- Browser used for manual tests: Edge 125
- Data source: MySQL
- Number of users affected: 20 (everyone who relies on the nightly file)

Relevant lines from the export log shown in the Admin > Jobs page:

- Checking the MySQL side: queries finish in under 5 seconds when run directly, so the database is not the bottleneck.

Our accountants have been reconciling payments manually since Thursday. The month-end close is in a few days and without the automated file we will not be able to finish on time. subject: Feature proposal: row-level security for embedded dashboards (detailed)
body:
Hello Kestrel product team,

I'd like to submit a detailed feature request. I'm the product manager at Saffron Kitchens and we have been using Kestrel on the Team plan for about two years. We are very happy with it, which is why we would like to keep using it for a project that is coming up.

Context
We are building a customer portal in which each of our clients should see analytics about their own activity. We would like to embed Kestrel dashboards in that portal instead of building our own charts. We have about 300 client accounts today and expect 1,000 within eighteen months.

The problem
Embedded dashboards currently show the same data to everyone who opens them. We cannot safely embed them because client A must never see client B's rows. Creating one dashboard per client is not workable with 300 (or 1,000) clients.

What we need
1. Row-level security: a filter on the data that is applied automatically based on an attribute of the viewer, for example a client_id claim in a signed embed token.
2. The filter must be enforced server-side. If it is only a URL parameter, a client could just edit it.
3. Ability to define the mapping once at dataset level rather than on every widget.
4. Audit information: which token/viewer opened which dashboard and when.
5. Reasonable behaviour when the attribute is missing (default: show nothing).

What we do today
We generate a PDF for each client every night with a script and email it. This works but is not interactive and clients keep asking for "live" numbers.

Alternatives we looked at
Two other BI tools offer this (I won't name them), one of them as an add-on. We would prefer to stay with Kestrel because our team already knows it, our data models are here and migration would cost us months. But our client portal launch is planned for the beginning of next year, so we need to make a decision in the next six to eight weeks.

Questions
- Is row-level security on your roadmap? If so, is there an approximate date?
- Is there an early access programme we could join? We would happily give feedback and provide test data.
- Is there an interim approach you would recommend and support?

Happy to jump on a call with our engineers to go through the details.

Best regards,
Anna Cohen
Product Manager, Saffron Kitchens

subject: Feature proposal: row-level security for embedded dashboards (detailed)
body:
Hello Kestrel product team,

I'd like to submit a detailed feature request. I'm the product manager at Marlowe Insurance and we have been using Kestrel on the Business plan for about two years. We are very happy with it, which is why we would like to keep using it for a project that is coming up.

Context
We are building a customer portal in which each of our clients should see analytics about their own activity. We would like to embed Kestrel dashboards in that portal instead of building our own charts. We have about 300 client accounts today and expect 1,000 within eighteen months.

The problem
Embedded dashboards currently show the same data to everyone who opens them. We cannot safely embed them because client A must never see client B's rows. Creating one dashboard per client is not workable with 300 (or 1,000) clients.

What we need
1. Row-level security: a filter on the data that is applied automatically based on an attribute of the viewer, for example a client_id claim in a signed embed token.
2. The filter must be enforced server-side. If it is only a URL parameter, a client could just edit it.
3. Ability to define the mapping once at dataset level rather than on every widget.
4. Audit information: which token/viewer opened which dashboard and when.
5. Reasonable behaviour when the attribute is missing (default: show nothing).

What we do today
We generate a PDF for each client every night with a script and email it. This works but is not interactive and clients keep asking for "live" numbers.

Alternatives we looked at
Two other BI tools offer this (I won't name them), one of them as an add-on. We would prefer to stay with Kestrel because our team already knows it, our data models are here and migration would cost us months. But our client portal launch is planned for the beginning of next year, so we need to make a decision in the next six to eight weeks.

Questions
- Is row-level security on your roadmap? If so, is there an approximate date?
- Is there an early access programme we could join? We would happily give feedback and provide test data.
- Is there an interim approach you would recommend and support?

Happy to jump on a call with our engineers to go through the details.

Please note that Carlos Lambert from our team is also following this ticket and may reply from a different address. Feel free to include them.

Best regards,
Marcus Andersson
Product Manager, Marlowe Insurance

curl -X POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query \

subject: Feature proposal: row-level security for embedded dashboards (detailed)
body:
Hello Kestrel product team,

I'd like to submit a detailed feature request. I'm the product manager at Ashgrove Pharma and we have been using Kestrel on the Starter plan for about two years. We are very happy with it, which is why we would like to keep using it for a project that is coming up.

Context
We are building a customer portal in which each of our clients should see analytics about their own activity. We would like to embed Kestrel dashboards in that portal instead of building our own charts. We have about 300 client accounts today and expect 1,000 within eighteen months.

The problem
Embedded dashboards currently show the same data to everyone who opens them. We cannot safely embed them because client A must never see client B's rows. Creating one dashboard per client is not workable with 300 (or 1,000) clients.

What we need
1. Row-level security: a filter on the data that is applied automatically based on an attribute of the viewer, for example a client_id claim in a signed embed token.
2. The filter must be enforced server-side. If it is only a URL parameter, a client could just edit it.
3. Ability to define the mapping once at dataset level rather than on every widget.
4. Audit information: which token/viewer opened which dashboard and when.
5. Reasonable behaviour when the attribute is missing (default: show nothing).

What we do today
We generate a PDF for each client every night with a script and email it. This works but is not interactive and clients keep asking for "live" numbers.

Alternatives we looked at
Two other BI tools offer this (I won't name them), one of them as an add-on. We would prefer to stay with Kestrel because our team already knows it, our data models are here and migration would cost us months. But our client portal launch is planned for the beginning of next year, so we need to make a decision in the next six to eight weeks.

Questions
- Is row-level security on your roadmap? If so, is there an approximate date?
- Is there an early access programme we could join? We would happily give feedback and provide test data.
- Is there an interim approach you would recommend and support?

Happy to jump on a call with our engineers to go through the details.

Best regards,
Lena Nguyen
Product Manager, Ashgrove Pharma

subject: Performance regression on dashboards since August 31 (measurements included)
body:
Hi team,

Since around August 31 our dashboards have become a lot slower. I measured a few of them so that you have numbers rather than "it feels slow". Everything below was measured in Edge 125, on a wired connection, with the browser cache cleared before each run, and the times are how long it takes until the last widget stops showing the loading spinner.

| Dashboard | Widgets | Time before (ms) | Time now (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing Funnel | 8 | 3000 | 14000 |
| Weekly KPIs | 4 | 5000 | 16000 |
| Marketing Funnel | 7 | 3000 | 27000 |
| Sales Overview | 7 | 3000 | 53000 |
| Finance Summary | 5 | 2000 | 24000 |
| Regional Revenue | 4 | 2000 | 37000 |
| Regional Revenue | 7 | 3000 | 41000 |
| Weekly KPIs | 6 | 2000 | 30000 |

Observations:
- The slowdown is much larger for dashboards with several widgets that use the same PostgreSQL data source.
- Dashboards that use uploaded CSV files are not affected at all.
- Opening a single widget in the editor and running its query is fast (under 2 seconds). It seems that the problem occurs when several widgets load at the same time, as if the queries were executed one after another instead of in parallel.
- The browser's network tab shows the requests to /api/widgets/query being started at almost the same time but the responses arriving one by one, about every 4 seconds.
- I checked with two colleagues in different offices and they see the same behaviour, so it isn't my machine or network.

What I'd like: confirmation of whether something changed on your side around that date (a new release or a change to query concurrency limits for our plan) and whether there is a setting we can change. If you need HAR files I can export them, but they contain our internal hostnames so I'd need to know how to send them securely.

It's not blocking us, people can still work, but the morning stand-up used to start with these dashboards and we now wait almost a minute for them.

Please note that Ingrid Weber from our team is also following this ticket and may reply from a different address. Feel free to include them.

We understand that you receive many requests. We are not asking for an immediate fix, only for a clear indication of where this stands and what we can expect.

Thanks a lot,
Anna Andersson
Marlowe Insurance

body:
Hello,

We are seeing intermittent failures on the Kestrel query API in production, starting around 09:15 UTC on September 7. Our own service depends on it to render analytics inside our product, so our end customers are seeing empty charts and error banners.

Summary
- Endpoint: POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query
- Symptom: HTTP 502 or 504, roughly one request out of three
- Before: error rate below 0.1% over the last three months
- Our client library: kestrel-python 3.2.1, default timeout 30s, 2 retries with exponential backoff
- Region: eu-west

Example request (values anonymised):

curl -X POST https://api.kestrel.example/v2/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KESTREL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dataset":"orders","metrics":["revenue"],"group_by":["month"],"limit":100}'

Typical failing response:

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","message":"upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers","request_id":"req_req_ad785bde"}}

Excerpt of our client-side log (UTC):

What we verified
- The problem is not tied to a specific dataset, we see it on 4 different datasets.
- It is not tied to payload size: tiny queries (limit 1) fail as well.
- It is not our network: the same request from three different networks behaves identically.
- Your status page shows all systems operational, which doesn't match what we observe.
- The retries help a bit but with three attempts we still get about 4% failures for end users.

We need to know whether this is a known incident and what the expected resolution time is, because we have to decide whether to put a maintenance banner in our product. Please also let us know if there's something we should change on our side (timeouts, concurrency).

Our team is spread over three time zones, so a written answer is more useful than a call. If a call is really needed, mornings (CET) work best.

For context, this is the third time in a few months that we run into something like this, and each time it took several days to get resolved. I'm not saying this to complain, I would just like to know whether there is a better channel for issues that affect production.

subject: Feature proposal: row-level security for embedded dashboards (detailed)
body:
Hello Kestrel product team,

I'd like to submit a detailed feature request. I'm the product manager at Redpine Software and we have been using Kestrel on the Free plan for about two years. We are very happy with it, which is why we would like to keep using it for a project that is coming up.

Context
We are building a customer portal in which each of our clients should see analytics about their own activity. We would like to embed Kestrel dashboards in that portal instead of building our own charts. We have about 300 client accounts today and expect 1,000 within eighteen months.

The problem
Embedded dashboards currently show the same data to everyone who opens them. We cannot safely embed them because client A must never see client B's rows. Creating one dashboard per client is not workable with 300 (or 1,000) clients.

What we need
1. Row-level security: a filter on the data that is applied automatically based on an attribute of the viewer, for example a client_id claim in a signed embed token.
2. The filter must be enforced server-side. If it is only a URL parameter, a client could just edit it.
3. Ability to define the mapping once at dataset level rather than on every widget.
4. Audit information: which token/viewer opened which dashboard and when.
5. Reasonable behaviour when the attribute is missing (default: show nothing).

What we do today
We generate a PDF for each client every night with a script and email it. This works but is not interactive and clients keep asking for "live" numbers.

Alternatives we looked at
Two other BI tools offer this (I won't name them), one of them as an add-on. We would prefer to stay with Kestrel because our team already knows it, our data models are here and migration would cost us months. But our client portal launch is planned for the beginning of next year, so we need to make a decision in the next six to eight weeks.

Questions
- Is row-level security on your roadmap? If so, is there an approximate date?
- Is there an early access programme we could join? We would happily give feedback and provide test data.
- Is there an interim approach you would recommend and support?

Happy to jump on a call with our engineers to go through the details.

Our team is spread over three time zones, so a written answer is more useful than a call. If a call is really needed, mornings (CET) work best.

Best regards,
Zoe Lambert
Product Manager, Redpine Software
